Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

**Overall recommendation:** Do not accept the Seller’s package as settled. It materially shifts pre-Completion business, financing and execution risk to Wattlebridge, despite the agreed AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free transaction. The Seller’s assertions about market practice and principal-level agreement should be verified with the deal team, not treated as established facts. We have only the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter, not the complete SPA or underlying DD documents; the proposed drafting must be checked against those documents and the current diligence record.

The most urgent issues are **Bluefen consent, discharge of Riverlark at Completion, the treatment of completion bonuses, and the unresolved Ironquay IP and export incident**.

## 1. Completion and purchase-price risks

### Bluefen: protect the key customer relationship

Bluefen reportedly represents approximately **AUD 3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue**. The disclosure identifies a change-control consent requirement and associated conditions, but no final consent or evidence that those conditions have been met.

- **Buyer concern:** A reasonable-endeavours obligation and a bare written consent may leave the Buyer obliged to complete without a valid, effective and unconditional permission to proceed, or with conditions that damage the relationship.
- **Push back:** Make receipt **before Completion** of Bluefen’s valid written consent, with all applicable conditions satisfied or waived, a condition precedent. The consent should not amend the contract adversely or impose unacceptable obligations on the Company or Buyer without the Buyer’s approval. Require prompt access to correspondence and a long-stop date and termination right if the condition is not satisfied or waived. Confirm the precise requirements against DD-002.

### Riverlark: no post-Completion release

Approximately **AUD 3.2 million** remains outstanding and no final security discharge has been supplied.

- **Buyer concern:** A release after Completion is inconsistent with delivering the Company debt-free and exposes the Buyer to repayment, security and enforcement risk.
- **Push back:** Require a binding payoff and release arrangement before Completion, with the facility repaid from Completion proceeds directly to Riverlark and all security released at Completion. Obtain payoff figures, discharge documents and undertakings to complete any necessary registrations. Ensure the debt is deducted in the price mechanics without double counting. Review DD-003 for change-control and discharge requirements.

### Completion bonuses: prevent value leakage

The **AUD 420,000** of conditional employee bonuses is absent from the draft funds flow. Completion and continued-employment conditions matter; the disclosure does not establish whether related payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.

- **Buyer concern:** The Company could bear a transaction-related cost while the Seller receives the full price, undermining the economics of the bargain.
- **Push back:** Establish when and by whom each amount becomes payable and quantify applicable on-costs. Allocate the bonuses and relevant on-costs to the Seller through the Completion funds flow or an appropriate purchase-price adjustment, with payment and employee-eligibility mechanics addressed. Avoid double recovery.

### Supplier renewals: quantify rather than assume

The three related Sandbar renewals total **AUD 330,000**. The available disclosure does not establish whether they are accrued, unavoidable, terminable or ordinary course.

- **Push back:** Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, including timing, scope, cancellation rights and accrual. Apply the agreed debt-free/cash-free and any working-capital or specific adjustment mechanics to the facts; seek a specific adjustment or protection for pre-Completion liabilities or commitments outside the agreed ordinary-course baseline. Do not simply accept either that all AUD 330,000 is a Seller cost or that it is ordinary-course Buyer cost.

## 2. Specific diligence risks requiring protection

### Ironquay IP: payment alone is insufficient

DD-004 reportedly makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows **AUD 180,000 open**, but that is not independent proof of non-payment; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is included.

- **Buyer concern:** The Company’s ownership of potentially important developed materials is uncertain. An indemnity limited to one payment may not cover defective title, disputes, remediation, replacement or business interruption.
- **Push back:** Before Completion, verify all amounts due and paid, settle any outstanding fees at the Seller’s cost and obtain a properly executed confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory evidence of ownership, free of claims. Expand the specific indemnity to cover losses arising from the matter, including reasonable defence and remediation costs, with appropriate claim controls and survival. Check whether the materials are material to the product and whether third-party rights remain.

### Export/privacy incident: investigate without assuming breach or loss

A download link went to an unintended external address; the export **may** contain approximately 1,240 records. Access, exact scope, notification obligations and loss remain unresolved.

- **Buyer concern:** The incident could create investigation, notification, regulatory, contractual and remediation exposure even though neither unauthorised access nor a notifiable breach is established.
- **Push back:** Require the Seller to preserve evidence, investigate promptly, provide findings and legal assessment, and take appropriate containment and remediation steps. Address cooperation and responsibility for any required notifications. Seek a tailored indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related losses, including reasonable investigation and remediation costs, and consider a Completion condition or retention if the risk cannot be bounded before signing or Completion. Avoid a disclosure qualification that eliminates protection merely because the incident was identified.

### Other contracts

- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a notification obligation, not a demonstrated landlord-consent condition. Confirm timing, content and responsibility for notice; do not invent a consent requirement.
- **Mossvale:** The disclosed clause restricts assignment, not necessarily a share sale. Review the full contract and transaction steps for any applicable restriction; seek consent only if actually required or commercially prudent.

## 3. Liability, remedies and disclosure

The Seller’s proposed limits need to be considered as an integrated package, not accepted because the disclosure letter calls them “market”.

### General warranties

The proposed **20% cap is AUD 4.8 million**. Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000 individually**, aggregate more than **AUD 250,000**, and only the excess is recoverable; general claims expire after **18 months**.

- **Buyer concern:** The cap, excess-only basket and short period together can leave meaningful losses unrecovered. The thresholds may also defeat groups of related smaller losses.
- **Push back:** Seek a higher general cap, a lower or no de minimis, and a **tipping basket** under which the full qualifying amount is recoverable once the basket is exceeded. Seek a longer general warranty period, with clear rules permitting related claims to be aggregated and notified claims to continue beyond expiry. The final commercial position should reflect diligence, insurance and recourse, rather than an unsupported market assertion.

### Fundamental, tax and IP protection

- **Title and capacity:** Reject applying the general cap, basket and 18-month period. Seek a cap up to the **full purchase price**, no de minimis or basket, and a substantially longer survival period appropriate to the applicable limitation periods.
- **Tax:** Seek a specific tax covenant or indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with an appropriate longer survival period aligned to relevant assessment periods, and a higher or separate cap. Address tax refunds, conduct and double recovery.
- **IP:** Seek robust ownership, licence, infringement and material-contract warranties. Given the known Ironquay issue, preserve the separate targeted remedy rather than relying solely on general warranties.
- **Specific indemnities:** Negotiate caps, thresholds and survival expressly for Ironquay and the incident; do not allow general limitations to apply by default.

### Global limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 and the proposed all-claims default could extend limitations to **every type of claim**, potentially including debt, specific indemnities and other express obligations.

- **Push back:** Define the claims to which each limitation applies and expressly preserve payment obligations, specific indemnities, covenants, agreed Completion and price-adjustment remedies, and the fundamental and tax regimes. Preserve remedies for fraud and any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded. Review the complete drafting for overlaps and unintended exclusions; avoid assuming a general fraud carve-out alone cures the allocation of risk.

### Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, and to bar claims for matters known or merely discoverable by the Buyer or advisers.

- **Buyer concern:** Broad deemed disclosure and constructive knowledge can transfer unidentified risks to the Buyer and make negotiated warranties ineffective. The letter’s factual disclosures also do not themselves establish the Seller’s proposed legal conclusions.
- **Push back:** Limit qualifying disclosure to matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail** in the disclosure letter and clearly identified supporting documents to enable a reasonable buyer to assess their nature and scope. Reject blanket data-room and public-record disclosure and constructive knowledge based on discoverability. If an actual-knowledge qualification is unavoidable, confine it to identified individuals’ actual knowledge and define its effect narrowly. Preserve the negotiated specific indemnities and other expressly protected remedies regardless of disclosure or knowledge.

## 4. Title and Completion deliverables

DD-012 records Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares; it is useful evidence, but the disclosure expressly does not establish independent verification or resolve all title questions.

- **Push back:** Verify the current issued capital, share register and relevant corporate records; check for options, conversion rights, encumbrances and required transfer approvals. Obtain properly executed share transfers and Completion documents, releases of relevant security, and warranties that the Seller owns and can transfer all shares free of encumbrances. Ensure post-Completion register updates are required.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. **Make Bluefen consent and its conditions a genuine Completion condition**; require Riverlark repayment and security release at Completion.
2. **Fix the economics:** allocate the AUD 420,000 bonuses and applicable on-costs to the Seller, and investigate and correctly allocate Sandbar liabilities.
3. **Resolve or ring-fence Ironquay and the export incident** through evidence, remediation and tailored indemnities; consider a condition or retention for unresolved material risk.
4. **Rebuild the remedies package:** improve general thresholds and survival; establish separate fundamental, tax and specific-indemnity regimes; prevent global limitations from overriding them.
5. **Reject blanket disclosure and constructive knowledge**, and complete title and contract verification before committing to close.

The team should next obtain the full SPA, DD-002–DD-012, current funds flow and updated evidence of developments since 22 September 2026. Those materials may change both the risk assessment and the precise drafting.
